title: Finding FB2-REV-FND-000035: the test_dp83869.c SIGSEGV is caused by CMock dereferencing a hard-coded TMS570 peripheral address from the test, and the previously recorded attribution to testPHY_OperationModeGet was wrong

evidence: TOOLING. lldb is confirmed broken on this host, independently of this test: 'lldb --batch -o run -o "bt all" ./test_dp83869.out' dies at '(lldb) target create' with 'PLEASE submit a bug report', and the identical failure occurs on a two-line hello.c compiled in /tmp, so it is unrelated to this binary. ~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/ does not exist and the emitted diagnostics.log is zero bytes, so no crash report is recoverable. gdb is not installed; the predecessor's bin/gdb shim has a Python 3 syntax error at line 64. AddressSanitizer was re-tried and does hang, at the LINK step, because the shipped ':tools: :test_linker:' appends -flto and LTO plus ASAN deadlocks this toolchain. The technique that worked needs neither: a constructor-installed SIGSEGV/SIGBUS handler with SA_SIGINFO in sil/tools/sil_crash_trace.h, injected only by 'SIL_DEBUG=1' (which also strips -flto and adds -g -O0 -fno-omit-frame-pointer), printing si_addr and backtrace_symbols_fd() and then re-raising with the default handler so the exit status is unchanged. A secondary defect had to be fixed first: sil/run.sh was NOT idempotent, re-inserting its -include, -I and -D lines on every invocation until project.yml carried nine copies of the SIL include path. That is now fixed and verified idempotent over repeated runs, and it is recorded because it is exactly the kind of harness drift that produces irreproducible results. THE TRACE, obtained by running the built binary under a pty ('script -q /dev/null ./test_dp83869.out'), after 13 passing cases and 2 class-A failures: '=== SIL CRASH: signal 11 at fault address 0xfff7bc38 ==='; frame 2 UnityAssertEqualIntArray + 260; frame 3 IO_PinReset + 524; frame 4 PHY_ResetHardware + 40; frame 5 testPHY_HardwareReset + 88; frame 6 run_test + 168; frame 7 main + 1004. THE PREVIOUS ATTRIBUTION WAS WRONG. The earlier record blamed testPHY_OperationModeGet at line 897. Ceedling attributes a crash to whichever case was in flight when the process died, and because the runner aborts, every case after the faulting one is reported as crashed - which is why five separate cases were logged as crashed. The real faulting case is testPHY_HardwareReset, tests/unit/app/driver/phy/test_dp83869.c:885, whose first substantive statement is line 889. THE CAUSE. Line 889 reads 'IO_PinReset_Expect(&((gioPORT_t *)0xFFF7BC34u)->DOUT, 1u);'. 0xFFF7BC34 is the genuine TMS570 gioPORTA base address and is recorded in the repository's own committed HALCoGen input, conf/hcg/app.dil:1707 'DRIVER.GIO.VAR.GIO_BASE_PORTA.VALUE=0xFFF7BC34', so the constant is not invented and the test is correct on target. The expression evaluates to 0xFFF7BC38 (base plus offsetof(DOUT), the second uint32_t of gioPORT_t) and is only TAKEN by the test, never dereferenced by it. CMock, however, dereferences it: ':when_ptr: :compare_data' applies to IO_PinReset's TYPED pointer parameter 'volatile uint32_t* pRegisterAddress' (src/app/driver/io/io.h:107), so the generated mock emits UNITY_TEST_ASSERT_EQUAL_HEX32_ARRAY(Expected_pRegisterAddress, pRegisterAddress, 1, ...) (Mockio.c:480) and reads BOTH operands. 0xFFF7BC38 is a device address with no mapping on the host; reading it is the SIGSEGV, and the captured si_addr of 0xfff7bc38 is that exact address, which closes the loop. The production code meanwhile passes a valid host object: phy_cfg.h:65 defines PHY_IO_HW_RESET_REG_DOUT as (gioPORTA->DOUT) and dp83869.c:542 calls IO_PinReset(&PHY_IO_HW_RESET_REG_DOUT, PHY_HW_RESET_PIN), which in the SIL model resolves to &sil_gio.PORT[0].DOUT (sil/iface/HL_gio.h:50). The same pattern appears at test_dp83869.c:133, :135, :891. This DIRECTLY REFUTES the earlier record's statement that 'the crash is not caused by the test's hard-coded peripheral address 0xFFF7BC34u (that address is only taken, never dereferenced)'. CMock dereferences it on the test's behalf; that claim needed a stack trace rather than reasoning and is now settled against it.
impact: Bounded and worth stating precisely, because it is not a product risk. The driver is correct: dp83869.c:542 and :544 pass the address of the configured reset register to the driver API, which is what they must do. The SIL model is correct: sil/iface/HL_gio.h maps gioPORTA onto a real host object and that mapping works, as the fact that the code under test dereferences a valid pointer shows. The defect is that a test asserts against a TARGET peripheral address, and CMock dereferences it; on the target that address is mapped and the comparison reads two real registers, on the host it is unmapped and the same comparison faults. The consequence is that tests/unit/app/driver/phy/test_dp83869.c cannot be brought up on a host SIL harness, and it is therefore counted among the 5 remaining failures. The previous record also overstated the cost by reporting the whole file as 15/15 failed after the runner aborted; running it under a pty shows 13 cases genuinely pass and 2 fail with the known class-A message, which is a real improvement in the evidence even though the test is still not brought up. The cost of the three ways to 'fix' it was each rejected: mapping a SIL gioPORTA at 0xFFF7BC34 would fabricate the target register map the harness exists to be honest about not having and would create a false impression of having verified register placement; retargeting the test to gioPORTA->DOUT would delete the only thing that says which physical pin is reset and would silently convert a real check into a tautology; suppressing the comparison would weaken the assertion. The honest options are both product-owner decisions: accept that this test is target-only, or redesign it to be target-independent. Nothing here is a statement about the PHY, about register placement, or about reset behaviour on hardware; the harness verifies driver logic against upstream's own assertions and nothing else.
root_cause: The test encodes a target-only precondition - the physical address of a GIO port register - into an expectation, and the test framework dereferences it. ':when_ptr: :compare_data' is a request to compare pointed-to DATA, and CMock honours it for the typed pointer that IO_PinReset declares, emitting a 1-element array comparison that reads the pointed-to uint32_t from BOTH the expected and the actual address. On target both addresses are mapped peripheral registers, so the assertion reads two registers and compares them, which is what the test author intended. On the host the expected address, taken verbatim from the device's base address in conf/hcg/app.dil, is unmapped, so the very act of checking the expectation dereferences an invalid address. The fault is therefore in the interaction between a device-specific test fixture and a host-only execution environment, not in the product code, not in the SIL model, and not in CMock's own logic. It is aggravated by Ceedling's crash attribution, which names whichever case was in flight when the process died and thereby obscured the true faulting case for as long as the crash was untraced.
resolution:
STILL OPEN. Re-verified on 2026-09-30T00:00:00Z against the most recent full SIL host sweep and its per-test log: tests/unit/app/driver/phy/test_dp83869.c still fails, and it still fails the way this record describes. The file reports 15 of 15 cases as crashed after the runner aborts, which is the signature of a process that dies mid-file with Ceedling attributing the crash to whatever case was in flight - not fifteen independent failures.

THE CMock ARRAY-PLUGIN WORK DOES NOT REACH IT, and that was worth checking rather than assuming. The array plugin changes the comparison selected for a void* parameter from UNITY_TEST_ASSERT_EQUAL_PTR to UNITY_TEST_ASSERT_EQUAL_HEX8_ARRAY. The fault here is not on a void* parameter: it is on IO_PinReset's typed `volatile uint32_t *` parameter, so the array branch is not the branch this code takes and the plugin is inert for this file. The root cause stands exactly as recorded: the test encodes a target-only precondition, the address of a GIO port register, into an expectation, CMock honours :when_ptr: :compare_data for the typed pointer and dereferences it, and 0xFFF7BC38 is a TMS570 device address with no mapping on a host.

PRECISE UNBLOCK CONDITION - one of exactly two things, both product-owner decisions, neither of which is a test edit this corpus may make. Either: accept tests/unit/app/driver/phy/test_dp83869.c as a target-only test and exclude it from host runs, with that reason recorded on the exclusion; or: redesign the file so the reset pin is identified in a way a host harness can evaluate. The three ways of making it go green without one of those were each constructed and each rejected on evidence, and the rejections are recorded in this record's own impact field and are not restated as if they were options. Mapping a SIL gioPORTA at 0xFFF7BC34 would fabricate the register map the harness exists to be honest about not having; retargeting to gioPORTA->DOUT would delete the only statement of which physical pin is reset; suppressing the comparison would weaken the oracle.

WHAT WAS ACHIEVED AND STILL STANDS: the root cause is isolated with a captured stack trace and a fault address that names the exact dereferenced location, the earlier misattribution to testPHY_OperationModeGet is corrected to testPHY_HardwareReset, and the file's 13 genuinely-passing cases and 2 class-A failures are individually visible instead of being reported as 15 of 15 failed after an abort. human_approval_status remains pending, production_authorized remains false and product_verification_credit remains false.
